parsed.use_case: A pricing or resource-planning service may need to enumerate every allowed bundle of item sizes whose total exactly matches a requested quantity, with each item type available without a fixed per-type limit. The same structure appears when composing a target from reusable denominations or package sizes.
system_examples: Coin change and cash-register systems — enumerate ways to assemble a requested value from reusable coin denominations.
Manufacturing cut-list planners — enumerate combinations of standard stock lengths that exactly meet a required total length.
parsed.explanation: Backtracking explores candidate choices while keeping the partial sum at or below the target, and restricts later choices to avoid generating the same combination in different orders. Runtime is output-sensitive and can be exponential in the target and candidate set; unlike checking whether any solution exists, returning every combination necessarily costs at least the size of the output. This problem is mainly a teaching exercise for exhaustive search, though similar enumeration can support constrained planning tools.
